name: Dallas–Fort Worth
meta_title: Dallas–Fort Worth VHS and photo transfer
meta_description: Local VHS, camcorder, film, and photo digitizing in Dallas–Fort Worth, including Flower Mound, Lewisville, and Denton. Prices only when the shop publishes them.
intro: Dallas–Fort Worth is large enough that “a shop in the Metroplex” can mean an hour in the car. This page covers businesses whose own sites offer tape, film, or photo transfer and that sit in, or explicitly serve, Dallas, Fort Worth, Flower Mound, Lewisville, Denton, and Richardson.

Call before you drive. The hours below are copied from the business site and still go stale. Ask whether they can play your exact format, what a damaged tape costs, and whether you leave with a file you can copy. If you would rather ship a mixed box, use the mail-in comparison. Shipping the only copy of a wedding tape is a real risk: photograph the labels first.

businesses.name: Home Video Studio
businesses.delivery: Digital Video Archive, cloud folder, USB or thumb drive, and a DVD per VHS tape
businesses.hours: Monday–Friday 9:00 a.m.–11:30 a.m. and 1:30 p.m.–5:30 p.m.; Saturday 11:00 a.m.–2:00 p.m.
notes: The Flower Mound page is written by owner Bill Burrow. He says he personally handles VHS, VHS-C, Hi8, Video8, MiniDV, 8mm and Super 8, photos, slides, and audio at this studio, and that customers can also drop off Betamax, 16mm, negatives, U-matic, PAL or SECAM VHS, audio cassette, reel-to-reel, and DAT.

Digital delivery named on the page: Digital Video Archive, a secure cloud folder, or a USB or thumb drive. The page says each VHS tape can also be put on its own DVD, and that the studio can repair some damaged VHS before that transfer.

The page lists local drop-off and says it serves Flower Mound, Lewisville, Highland Village, Argyle, Grapevine, Coppell, Frisco, Keller, Fort Worth, Denton, Southlake, and nearby North Texas. It does not publish a dollar price. The page says to call (945) 295-6177.

businesses.name: Dead Set Digital
businesses.area: Flower Mound, Lewisville, and Denton pickup
businesses.source_label: Dead Set Digital VHS conversion page
businesses.turnaround: 7–10 days, as stated on the page
businesses.delivery: Digital files; DVD copies are an add-on
notes: The service page offers VHS-to-digital conversion with free pickup and delivery in Flower Mound, Denton, Lewisville, Highland Village, Trophy Club, Argyle, Northlake, and The Colony. It does not publish a street address. The phone is (214) 500-7174. The page is written in the first person and says the tapes are handled by the operator, who describes himself as based in Denton.

Published VHS rates on that page: $30 per tape for 1–4 tapes, and packages “as low as $22.50 per tape.” A comparison table on the same page lists $250 for 10 tapes, which is $25 a tape, not $22.50. The page also names a 5-tape package and a 20-tape bin special without a price in the text. Ask for those rates.

Add-ons listed in text: DVD copies +$5 per tape, basic editing +$10, and rush service +$10 for a 3-day turnaround. A +$15 flat fee is also printed beside the rush lines. The page layout does not make clear what the $15 covers. Standard turnaround is stated as 7–10 days. The page says pickup can be Tuesday or Thursday.
This listing does not repeat the customer quotes on that page. This directory did not contact those people.

businesses.name: The Panhandle House
businesses.source_label: Digital Transfer Services video price list

price_lines.label: DVD master, in addition to the transfer

businesses.delivery: Digital transfer; a DVD or Blu-ray master is a separate charge
notes: Digital Transfer Services at The Panhandle House publishes a consumer price list at 313 N. Locust St., Denton, TX 76201, phone (940) 349-9229. The page requires a 50% deposit with the order.
A DVD master is $14.95 on top of the transfer and holds about two hours. Tapes longer than 120 minutes are split across more than one disc. Additional disc copies are $9.95.

The same page prices professional cassettes separately: S-VHS, U-matic, BetaSP, and DVCPRO or DVCam, with a higher rate past 60 minutes. Memory cards and hard-drive camcorders are “ask for a quote.” The page does not state a turnaround time or a photo-scanning service.

businesses.name: WeScanFilm
businesses.source_label: What We Digitize, including photo rates

extra_sources.label: Video tape formats and MiniDV capture

businesses.service_mode: In-studio drop-off, or ship to the studio
businesses.price_summary: Photos from $0.27; tapes quoted per project
businesses.delivery: USB or hard drive, or a cloud download; MP4 mentioned for tapes
businesses.hours: Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; Saturday by appointment
notes: WeScanFilm publishes the studio address as 12805 Harmon Rd, Suite 215, Fort Worth, TX 76177, phone (214) 519-9637, email info@wescanfiles.com. Hours on the services page and the VHS page are Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m., Saturday by appointment.

The services page lists photo scanning, restoration, slides and negatives, scrapbooks, VHS and video tapes, movie reels, maps, and posters. Photo rates above are the “from” prices at 600 DPI, and the page says every collection is quoted and approved before work starts. It says film, tape, reel, and large-format work is quoted per project rather than from a fixed tape menu.

The VHS page says they transfer VHS and VHS-C in house, deliver files on a flash drive, an external hard drive, or a cloud link, and return the original tapes. It says they also transfer MiniDV and Hi8. The tape page says MiniDV is captured over FireWire and that finished files are encoded to MP4. Cities named on the VHS page include Fort Worth, Haltom City, Arlington, Keller, Southlake, Grapevine, North Richland Hills, Roanoke, Denton, and Dallas.
The services page says the studio has preserved family history for nearly 20 years. This listing does not repeat a specific tape price that is not on these current pages.

businesses.name: EGAMI A/V
businesses.source_label: EGAMI A/V media conversion price list
businesses.service_mode: Fort Worth shop; mail return is extra
businesses.price_summary: First tape $25; later tapes $10 plus 13¢ a minute

price_lines.label: First VHS, VHS-C, Video8, Hi8, or Digital8

businesses.delivery: MP4 or DVD for video; MP3 or CD for audio; files can be emailed
notes: EGAMI A/V publishes this rate card for 5664 Rockport Lane, Fort Worth, TX 76137, phone (817) 577-2564, email info@egamitapes.com. The page is signed by Blake Stiles and describes a small shop. It says they cannot duplicate copyrighted material.

A DVD is capped at two hours, and an audio CD at 78 minutes. Orders over 15 tapes are told to call for a bulk discount. Digital files can be emailed at no extra charge. Discs and original media returned by mail are subject to postage. The page says to call if you want both files and DVDs, because that can be an additional charge.

A later tape of 120 minutes is $10 plus $15.60, or $25.60, using the published 13¢-per-minute rate. That is arithmetic from the card, not a separate package they advertise. The page does not list MiniDV or a turnaround time.

businesses.name: Fort Worth Camera / The Print Refinery
businesses.turnaround: Not published — the page says “after some time”
businesses.delivery: DVD, Blu-ray, USB, or cloud, as the page describes it
notes: Fort Worth Camera’s video page, also labeled The Print Refinery, gives the address 6483 Camp Bowie Boulevard, Fort Worth, TX 76116, and the phone 817-335-3456. It names 1980s VHS and 8mm movie film and says they work with most video media. The how-it-works list also includes audio.

The introduction says finished footage can go to DVD, Blu-ray, a USB drive, or cloud storage. The step list says to choose DVD or USB. Originals are returned. The page says the print lab has been preserving memories for over 23 years, and that some exceptions apply.
No price and no day count are published on this page. Ask for both, and ask which formats beyond VHS and 8mm film they currently run.

businesses.name: Action Video Service
businesses.turnaround: Less than a week for a small VHS order, as they describe their average
businesses.hours: Monday and Friday 9:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; Tuesday and Thursday 9:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m.; Saturday 9:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m. Closed Wednesday and Sunday.
notes: Action Video Service lists 819 W. Arapaho Rd., Suite 23, Richardson, TX 75080, phone 972-437-2021. The homepage says they transfer VHS to DVD, archive to digital MP4, and transfer 8mm, Super 8, and 16mm, including PAL and SECAM cassettes.
They write that a small VHS order averages less than a week, and that originals come back at no charge. The page says to call for pricing. It does not publish a rate card.

They say they serve the Metroplex, and the city list on the page includes Dallas, Fort Worth, Arlington, Flower Mound, and Denton, among others. The browser title mentions photo and slide transfers. The body text fetched for this listing does not describe still-image scanning or a price for it. Ask if that is what you need.
The page says they will not transfer adult content.

businesses.name: Amni Video Transfer
notes: Amni Video Transfer lists 11722 Marsh Lane, Dallas, TX 75229, and the phone 469-557-8000. The page says they convert VHS, Hi8, MiniDV, and more, and the headline also names Super 8, 8mm film transfer, and photo scanning in the DFW area.
Delivery named on the page is a USB drive or an external hard drive. The page says prices are competitive and does not publish a number, a turnaround, or hours.
